Official Liner-Note Narrative (2004 / 2007)

Before the Distance: The Story of John & Erin

A Five-Song Twin Narrative Published by Ryan & Cassidy O'Connell

Originally conceived by Ryan and Cassidy O'Connell in 1986 and published in the liner booklet of 2004's Progress Street (with its concluding vault chapters restored on 2007's Lost Sounds), the story of fraternal twins John and Erin—both of whom use heavy-duty motorized power wheelchairs to navigate the steep, hilly Ironstone campus of Commonwealth Polytechnic Institute (CPI)—is one of The Stardust Engine's most famous pieces of in-universe fiction, portrayed visually by Ryan and Cassidy themselves.

I & II. The Skip Button at Kincaid Hall

Track 3: Seconds Into Forever Track 4: Thunder in the Rain

Fraternal twins John and Erin (portrayed in the liner-note photography by Ryan and Cassidy O'Connell) grew up sharing an unspoken frequency. Because the Blacksburg plateau and the Commonwealth Polytechnic Institute (CPI) campus are carved into steep Appalachian hills—from the sweeping oval of Commonwealth Green up to Faraday Hall on the Engineering Quad—both John and Erin use heavy-duty motorized power wheelchairs to navigate the five-percent campus grades. Where Erin was instinctive, fierce, and fiercely protective, John was quiet, analytical, and gentle—a CPI systems engineering undergraduate who trusted people at face value and assumed that everyone operated by the same honest rules he did.

In the autumn of their sophomore year in Blacksburg, Erin talked John into attending a Friday night campus speed-dating mixer in the Kincaid Hall Second-Floor Lounge. The rules were simple: each round lasted exactly three minutes. To time the rotations without a harsh buzzer, the student organizer had cued up a three-minute, 85-BPM romantic power ballad called "Seconds Into Forever"—a gentle, shimmering song built around the promise that "It only takes three minutes to believe!"

The Fatal Track Skip: "Thunder in the Rain"

"The clock on the wall is a guillotine blade / Cutting down the promises we never made... The neon signs are flashing 'Danger' in red / But I'd rather be living than safe and dead / Hold on tight, baby, don't let go / We're dancing on the edge of the volcano!"

Just as a striking, charismatic graduate student named Valerie sat down at Table 4 across from John's power wheelchair, the flustered student running the sound system accidentally fat-fingered the skip button on the CD deck—bypassing Track 3 ("Seconds Into Forever") and blasting Track 4: "Thunder in the Rain."

For ten deceptive seconds, a lush, cinematic analog brass-synth swell filled the room. Then, at 150 BPM in C minor, the guitars and drums detonated. Instead of rotating or laughing off the mistake, Valerie leaned in, locking eyes with John over the roaring chorus and telling him that the universe had skipped the polite ballad because the two of them were meant for the storm. Crucially, John did not realize he was looking at his future abuser. Blinded by the pounding adrenaline of the song and the overwhelming intensity of her attention, he mistook a textbook predatory love-bombing ambush for destiny—completely missing that the lyrics blasting from the speakers were literally flashing "Danger" in red.

III. The Executive Decision on Commonwealth Mall

Track 8: Before the Distance

Once the trap closed, the isolation was surgical. Within weeks of that speed-dating mixer, Valerie moved into John's orbit and began systematically cutting every wire that connected him to safety. She made him feel guilty whenever he called Erin. She monitored his classes at Faraday Hall, degraded his confidence behind closed doors, and convinced him that her suffocating control was what adult romance required him to endure.

By late November 2004, John was a ghost of himself. Every Blue Ridge Transit bus on campus met in a chaotic, bumper-to-bumper curbside lineup along Commonwealth Mall, idling in a diesel-choked gauntlet between Kincaid Hall, Pendleton Library, and the vaulted Ironstone arches of The Keystone Bridge. When Erin finally managed to arrange a brief meetup with her brother on a freezing, rain-slicked evening beneath the stone arch of The Keystone Bridge, John didn't arrive alone. Valerie stood right beside his power wheelchair in the driving rain, her fingers dug possessively into his wet rain-jacket sleeve, answering questions on his behalf while John stared at the wet pavement with his hand limp beside his joystick controller.

Lyrics Excerpt: "Before the Distance" (Sung by Cassidy as Erin)

"I saw the shadow falling across your face / A quiet surrender in a crowded place / You wore a mask, but the edges were frayed / Lost in the rules of a game that we played..."

"When the steel doors close and the platform clears / You can hear the truth grinding in the gears... Logic is a cage when the danger is real / You can't code the panic, you can't fake what you feel / I'm turning around, I'm breaking the track / Whatever it costs me, I'm taking it back!"

Through the chaotic wall of idling buses, hazards, and rushing umbrellas along Commonwealth Mall, a southbound Blue Ridge Transit Route 1 low-floor city bus (1 FALLING BRANCH) hissed to a stop at the boarding curb, its amber LED headboard reflecting off the puddles as the front pneumatic suspension kneeled and the yellow-bordered aluminum ADA wheelchair ramp deployed from the front boarding door onto the wet concrete. Because John and Erin shared a ground-floor accessible apartment on Progress Street NE—just two blocks from Commonwealth Mall—they never needed a bus to get home. Instead, Valerie was insisting that John board the southbound bus with her to spend the weekend isolated at her off-campus apartment down the Route 1 corridor in Christiansburg.

Seeing the terror and quiet surrender in her twin brother's eyes as Valerie tried to guide his power wheelchair toward the deployed front-door ramp, Erin realized with sudden, chilling clarity that if she let John board that bus and let those steel doors close—if she traded her courage for polite little lies and rolled the two blocks home to Progress Street NE alone—the distance would swallow him whole.

As Valerie stepped onto the bottom edge of the aluminum ramp and ordered John to roll aboard, Erin made an executive decision: John was coming home instead. Driving her power wheelchair forward across the wet bricks of the Commonwealth Mall sidewalk, Erin wedged her heavy steel frame directly between John's chair and the front boarding ramp, locking her brakes and covering John's cold hand on his joystick with her own. Refusing to yield the sidewalk despite Valerie's furious demands that John get on the bus, Erin held a locked perimeter on the curb until John reversed his chair away from the ramp and the steel doors hissed shut without him—then escorted her twin brother side by side the two blocks down the sidewalk to the safety of their apartment on Progress Street NE.

IV. The Twin's Safe Harbor

Lost Sounds • Track 13: Sanctuary in the Storm

Getting off the Commonwealth Mall sidewalk was only the physical extraction; surviving the aftermath required a sanctuary. Two blocks away, inside the warmth of their ground-floor accessible apartment on Progress Street NE—with their two power wheelchairs charging side by side in the hallway, John's buzzing flip phone powered off inside a ceramic cookie jar, and the deadbolt locked against the November storm—the psychological vault inside John's chest finally swung open.

Lyrics Excerpt: "Sanctuary in the Storm" (Duet: Ryan as John & Cassidy as Erin)

[John]: "I was lost inside a silent scream / Living out a fractured dream / A ship without a sail, adrift at sea / Thought the darkness was a part of me..."

[Erin & John]: "You are my sanctuary in the storm / A fire here to keep me safe and warm / When the thunder rolls and the cold winds blow / I'll never let you go / We are a sanctuary in the storm."

For weeks, as Valerie raged and tried every manipulative tactic to lure him back, Erin stood as an immovable firewall. In the quiet safety of his fraternal twin sister's home, John learned that love was never supposed to feel like a cage, and that he didn't have to endure darkness to deserve connection.

V. The Circle Completed

Lost Sounds • Track 14: Not Her

The following spring, the twins' roles reversed. Outside the Kincaid Hall Auditorium after an evening research symposium, a slick, practiced predator named Marcus cornered Erin's power wheelchair in a recessed Ironstone alcove—planting his boot on the base of the ramp to block her turning radius and deploying the exact same charming, isolating script that had once trapped John ("A girl as brilliant as you shouldn't have to play caretaker just because you share a birthday...").

Lyrics Excerpt: "Not Her" (Duet: Ryan as John & Cassidy as Erin)

[Erin]: "Brother, listen, something's wrong / We've been here for far too long / His eyes are cold, his words are cheap / A poisoned promise he can't keep / Just take my hand, let's turn and run / Before his wicked game is won!"

[John]: "I know your game, I know your kind / The little traps you leave behind... I've walked through fire, I've paid the cost / And I won't let another light be lost / Not her. Not today. Not ever again!"

Because John had walked through that fire and paid the cost, his analytical mind recognized the predator's routine in a fraction of a second. Thumb-shifting his power wheelchair into its highest outdoor climbing gear, John drove straight up the concrete incline and wedged two hundred and fifty pounds of rolling steel and battery torque directly between Marcus and Erin's chair. Dismantling Marcus's script to his face with surgical fury, John forced him to retreat into the rain—rescuing his twin sister outside Kincaid Hall just as she had rescued him along Commonwealth Mall.

Cross-Universe Narrative Echoes

Because Ryan and Cassidy O'Connell published the story of John and Erin inside the liner booklet of Progress Street in October 2004, fans of The Stardust Engine across the interconnected RaggieSoft universe read this exact story—turning these songs into a real-world warning flare when predators entered their own lives.

The Rachel Narrative • Nov 2006

Jessica's Train Ride: Kent Station vs. Commonwealth Mall

In November 2006, at Kent Station in Washington State, Jessica sees the frayed, exhausted shadow on her brother Michael's face as he stands on the platform beside his abuser, Delores. Unlike Erin along Commonwealth Mall, Jessica hesitates—boarding the commuter train to Seattle King Street Station alone and letting the pneumatic steel doors hiss shut without pulling Michael aboard.

Moments later, when "Before the Distance" comes on shuffle on her pre-release Quantum Zephyr media player, Jessica remembers reading The Stardust Engine's story of John and Erin. Realizing in horror that she and Michael are living out the exact same story—except she failed to make Erin's executive decision before the doors closed—Jessica weeps openly in her wheelchair bay all the way to Seattle and immediately dispatches Andromeda to try to extract him.

CPI Campus Lore • Freddie & Paige

Freddie & Paige: The Warning Inside "Thunder in the Rain"

After seeing Ryan and Cassidy O'Connell perform live in Kincaid Hall during their CPI freshman orientation, Freddie and Paige devoured The Stardust Engine's discography and liner notes—including the published booklet story of how John met his abuser at a Kincaid Hall speed-dating event when the organizer accidentally skipped past "Seconds Into Forever" and played "Thunder in the Rain" instead.

When "Thunder in the Rain" later echoes across campus, Freddie and Paige find themselves wondering why they have heard that exact song before—before connecting the 150-BPM stadium anthem to the liner-note story of John's speed-dating ambush and recognizing how predators use chaos and noise to mask their approach.
